title: From Perils to Possibilities: Understanding how Human (and AI) Biases affect Online Fora

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing opinion dynamics models (e.g., Bounded Confidence models) and network simulations to evaluate how platform recommender systems systematically skew interactions towards like-minded individuals and foster polarization.

Analyzing mathematical models of social learning, network measures of homophily/acrophily, and LLM-agent simulations configured via prompt engineering to study opinion fragmentation and echo chamber formation.

Reviewing top-down behavioral approaches, specifically the use of cognitive network models of semantic memory built from LLM-generated data to investigate structural biases (including racial, gender, and STEM-related stereotypes) in language representations.

Reviewing agent-based social movement simulations that evaluate the inherent tendencies of LLMs to produce more polite, respectful, and consensus-driven dialogue compared to real-world human social media users.
